newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firm on foreign buying, curve steepens.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firm on foreign buying, curve steepens.

text.p: Irish bonds were buoyed by foreign buying on Wednesday as European markets pushed ahead following the Federal Reserve's overnight decision to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged, dealers said.
Dealers said the Irish market had seen some curve steepening. It had traded roughly in line with Bunds but underperformed other peripheral European bond markets, they said.
"It's been very much a case of Europe pushing ahead, following no hike from the Fed," one dealer said. "There's been good buying today of all non-core markets."
By 1500 GMT the eight percent bond due 2000 was up 23p at 105.10 to yield 6.43 percent, while the eight percent bond due 2006 was up 35p at 106.05, to yield 7.00 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were trading at around 101 basis points over Bunds in the 10-year area, where the spread was still having difficulty making a decisive break below 100 basis points.
"Although we are trading very much in line with Bunds we are underperforming other peripherals," one said. "But there has been good interest in the market from foreign buyers."
He said a British auction of ultra-long gilts had gone well, giving a slight boost to the Irish market.
Dealers said attention was now focused on the performance of U.S. Treasuries.
